root_cause: The modal's focus trap only forces focus back to the modal element when focus leaves, but does not handle Tab/Shift+Tab key wrapping among the dialog's focusable elements. When the modal opens, the modal element (tabindex=-1) receives focus; the first Tab moves to the close button, but Shift+Tab from the close button would normally return to the modal element instead of wrapping to the last focusable element (Delete button).
repair_strategy: Add a keydown event listener on the modal element that intercepts Tab and Shift+Tab keys while the modal is shown. The handler computes the first and last focusable elements in the dialog and moves focus accordingly, preventing the default browser behavior.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate the modal dialog using Tab and Shift+Tab with proper focus wrapping between the first and last focusable controls, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: The generic focusable selector may include unintended elements if the dialog structure changes.
The new keydown listener could conflict with other keydown handlers on the modal element.
verification_requirements: Open the delete confirmation modal, press Tab to reach the close button, then press Shift+Tab and verify focus moves to the Delete button.
Press Tab from the Delete button and verify focus wraps to the close button.
Ensure Escape key still closes the modal.
